findings.message: `settle_triage` skips every accepted decision whose `lifecycle_id` differs from `self.lifecycle_id`. Each drain or serve process builds a fresh uuid lifecycle (`build_control`), including after a crash restart or a self-upgrade re-exec handoff. So a triage request that `consume` accepted and journaled before the process ended, but that never reached an idle point, is never applied: the operator was told `triage submitted: <id>` and the pass never runs. The ticket says settle mirrors `settle_admissions` (which applies accepted requests regardless of lifecycle) and relies on the `triage/<request_id>` Effects key so that 'a repeated settle or a restart never runs it twice'. That wording assumes an accepted, unapplied request survives a restart. Lifecycle staleness is already enforced at `consume`, which journals requests from other lifecycles as `stale`, so the extra filter only drops valid accepted work.
findings.paved_road: Drop the `body["lifecycle_id"] != self.lifecycle_id` condition in `settle_triage`, as `settle_admissions` does, and let the `triage/<request_id>` effect key give once-only application. Add a unit case where a decision accepted under lifecycle `old` is settled exactly once by an inbox whose lifecycle is `live`.
